P001.text: Act on overlapping customer histories: dated order sequences and, for a limited consenting sample, reconstructed sequences of receipt or collection, product use, stock remaining, attempted refilling and subsequent purchase.

P002.text: Order dates provide calendar anchors; recalled events may have uncertain dates, omitted episodes or unusual quantities.

P003.text: Sample both repeat purchasers and nonpurchasers across fulfillment options, starter versus existing containers, discounts and acquisition periods.

P004.text: Shared service conditions might produce recurring temporal patterns, but neither comparable household consumption nor a common response to those conditions is established.

P005.text: During week one, construct a calendar-dated order reference and separate weekly event sequences for participating households.

P006.text: Use one voluntary invitation offering an interview and optional agreed follow-up; do not repeatedly contact nonrespondents.

P007.text: Ask about actual use, remaining stock, alternative purchases and service encounters without presuming dissatisfaction.

P008.text: Preserve unknown intervals and distinguish reported events from recorded orders.

P009.text: Compare overlapping histories, shifting only uncertain recalled segments within their reported date ranges until distinctive ordered patterns correspond across several independently anchored histories.

P010.text: Keep known order dates fixed, preserve event order, and compare alternative alignments rather than selecting the most convenient one.

P011.text: For example, test whether uncertain recollections of a failed collection fall into a consistently dated sequence of low stock, collection difficulty and delayed purchase.

P012.text: Also compare time since first order and since reported depletion, without replacing calendar dates.

P013.text: Where a mismatch suggests a missing episode, seek clarification through an already agreed follow-up; do not insert an event merely to improve the match.

P014.text: Stop alignment when alternatives remain equally plausible, overlap is insufficient or the first week ends.

P015.text: If a recurring, corroborated sequence identifies an actionable fulfillment or communication obstacle, choose one corresponding process change for the remaining month: for example, clearer refill instructions for evidenced confusion, or a feasible collection-hours adjustment for evidenced access difficulty.

P016.text: Prespecify its intended observable effect and, where feasible, randomly allocate eligible customers or collection periods to the changed process and the current process.

P017.text: If no explanation is sufficiently discriminated, stop short of choosing a purported remedy and use the purchasing deadline to make a cautious, explicitly uncertain commitment from confirmed orders and reported stock needs.

P018.text: Look for one permissible alignment that repeatedly matches distinctive sequences across independently anchored households and makes previously inconsistent timing intelligible.

P019.text: Record whether competing alignments also fit.

P020.text: A candidate signal could be low stock followed by an unsuccessful collection attempt and a later order, recurring around the same service conditions; another could be continued stock availability without a refill attempt.

P021.text: These are proposed observations, not findings.

P022.text: Apparent missing or anomalous episodes become questions for corroboration, not established facts.

P023.text: During the trial, observe the specific targeted step—such as successful collection or correct completion of refilling—alongside remaining stock, attempted purchases and dated orders.

P024.text: Record participation and missing follow-up separately from outcomes.

P025.text: A distinctive, independently corroborated alignment can narrow the calendar position of uncertain customer events, check reconstructed histories and connect overlapping observation periods.

P026.text: It can thereby distinguish some households that have not yet needed a refill from households whose need preceded a documented obstacle.

P027.text: Repeated correspondence supports prioritizing a mechanism for a bounded trial; it does not establish that the mechanism explains the overall decline.

P028.text: A credible comparison during the month can support a provisional decision about the changed process within the tested group and conditions.

P029.text: At five weeks, base the purchasing commitment on confirmed demand, observed stock and usage information, trial results and explicit uncertainty.

P030.text: Use any consented later observation to assess second orders once cohorts have actually completed eight weeks.

P031.text: Household size, usage, initial quantity, alternative purchasing and local service events can disrupt shared patterns.

P032.text: Short, repetitive sequences, recall and measurement errors, incorrect anchors, insufficient overlap and searching many shifts can create false matches.

P033.text: Do not claim precise dates when only a range is supported, or extend a chronology beyond supported overlaps.

P034.text: Promotions and new collection points began in the same quarter, so matching timing alone cannot separate their effects.

P035.text: Voluntary participants and support-message senders may differ from other customers; neither complaint frequency, silence nor nonpurchase directly measures satisfaction.

P036.text: A month's trial cannot establish eight-week repeat purchase for newly exposed customers, and small or nonrandom comparisons may remain inconclusive.

P037.text: Stop or revise the trial if it creates observed fulfillment problems or cannot be delivered as specified; document departures before interpreting outcomes.

P038.text: Major packaging redesign is unavailable, and evidence of leaks may warrant further investigation without implying that the permitted process change will resolve them.
